episodes.summary: Daily 5 min cyber security news summary. News, patches, vulnerabilities and trends in information and network security. SANS Stormcast Thursday, November 12th, 2026: Apache mod_http2 RCE (CVE-2026-119618); Fortinet FortiMail Criticals; Ivanti EPM SQLi (CVE-2026-121653); Windows SignDrop CLFS; N-able N-central HF2

show_notes.heading: This episode covers leftover Patch Tuesday issues: a critical remote code execution flaw in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module (CVE-2026-119618), Fortinet's 89 advisories with 17 critical vulnerabilities especially in FortiMail, Ivanti's November 2026 update including an Endpoint Manager SQL injection and a Cloud Services Application certificate issue, an unpatched Windows Common Log File System privilege escalation called SignDrop, and N-able's N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2.
Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-119618)

Apache released HTTP Server 2.4.71, fixing a critical heap overflow in the mod_http2 assign_headers function that can lead to remote code execution. No public working exploit is available yet; disabling HTTP/2 can mitigate the issue, but proxies that translate to HTTP/2 still need to watch for HTTP request smuggling.
Fortinet November Advisories

Fortinet published 89 advisories addressing more than 100 vulnerabilities across its product portfolio, including 17 rated critical. FortiMail received the most critical fixes, and several of the critical issues may allow unauthenticated arbitrary code execution. Fortinet used AI as part of the vulnerability discovery work behind this release.
Ivanti November 2026 Security Update

Ivanti's November 2026 security update includes a SQL injection in Endpoint Manager (EPM) that may be leveraged for remote code execution, tracked as CVE-2026-121653, and a vulnerability in Ivanti Cloud Services Application (CSA) that allowed unauthenticated alteration of trusted EPM Core certificates (CVE-2026-121683).
Windows SignDrop CLFS Privilege Escalation

Researcher Nightmare Eclipse (MSNightmare) released SignDrop, a local privilege escalation in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) that abuses the HMAC-based log-file authentication Microsoft added about a year ago, along with symlink and timing tricks. A regular user can escalate to SYSTEM on Windows 11 26H2 and Windows Server 2025. A proof-of-concept is on GitHub; Microsoft has not confirmed the issue, there is no CVE, and disabling CLFS log authentication is not a recommended workaround because it would restore older CLFS attacks.
N-able N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2

N-able has released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2, and the release notes identify three CVE numbers addressed in the update, after N-able earlier shut down its hosted infrastructure in response to the reported vulnerabilities. The initial public reports described around 30 vulnerabilities, and attackers are already probing leaked paths. Shadowserver's count of exposed N-central servers dropped from about 1,338 to around 148. On-premises operators should apply the hotfix before bringing a server back online and still avoid exposing it if possible.

show_notes.heading: Microsoft's November Patch Tuesday, Apple's iOS and macOS updates, and SAP's Security Patch Day all arrived this week, including an already exploited Outlook spoofing bug and four SAP flaws with a perfect CVSS score of 10.
Microsoft Patch Tuesday

Microsoft is addressing 1,260 vulnerabilities this month, 68 of them critical, including 167 Chromium issues that affect Microsoft Edge. One already exploited Outlook spoofing vulnerability, CVE-2026-124194, may hide the risk of a file being opened, in a Mark of the Web style issue, though Microsoft does not rate it critical. Other notable critical issues include a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) remote code execution flaw in Active Directory environments (CVE-2026-119958), five critical Microsoft Queuing and Queue Manager bugs, and a Windows TCP/IP remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-113859) that Microsoft rates critical despite a 7.5 Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score.
Apple Patches

Apple released updates for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS that fix only nine vulnerabilities, with iPadOS and macOS patches going back to version 18, watchOS one version back, and visionOS only for the current release. Most of the issues weaken the Bluetooth handshake so an attacker can pair with a phone or Mac, and there are also AirPlay rate-limiting problems; one vulnerability only affects an older iOS release and lets an attacker with physical access pair a locked device with an AirPlay receiver. A more notable iMessage issue may let someone join a group and receive its messages without being invited. Apple states that none of these bugs are being exploited.
SAP Patch Tuesday

SAP's November Security Patch Day, issued in sync with Microsoft's, includes four vulnerabilities with a perfect CVSS score of 10, three more at 9.9, and two more in the nines, including issues in SAP NetWeaver. Onapsis reported a broken access control flaw in SAP Gateway (CVE-2026-89103) tied to the proxy access control list, and a WebSocket memory-corruption bug that Onapsis has shown as a denial of service but says can also allow remote code execution (CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126).

Attackers Searching for SAP NetWeaver Webshells

ISC honeypots are seeing probes for ant.jsp and related paths tied to SAP NetWeaver CVE-2025-31324, a CVSS 10 unauthenticated file-upload flaw attackers still use to plant webshells even after recent patches. Watch /irj/servlet_jsp/irj/root/ and other upload endpoints for leftover shells.
N-able N-central Critical Security Incident

Google Chrome Zero-Day Patch (CVE-2026-125350)

Chrome stable updates fix nine vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-125350, a use-after-free in the XML parser that Google says is already exploited in the wild. Update promptly; the advisory does not confirm a sandbox escape.
Strict Outlook DMARC Policies
Outlook is rejecting mail with 550 errors when the sending domain lacks a DMARC record, even if SPF and DKIM pass. Publish at least a DMARC record (for example p=none) alongside SPF and DKIM.

ISC honeypots saw Cisco IOS vulnerability scans from exposure-management firm RootEvidence. Unlike typical Internet-wide scanners, their HTTP requests include Opt-Out-Email and Opt-Out-Url headers so administrators can request exclusion.
OpenSSH musl Password Bypass (sshole / CVE-2026-123158)

A critical password-authentication bypass affects OpenSSH on musl libc systems (Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, and similar) when sshd allows password logins without libpam. Passwords longer than 256 characters can authenticate accounts that have no password set (shadow field "*"). Details and walkthrough at sshhole.com; fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2.
Guidance to Secure Refrigeration / Cold-Chain Systems

U.S. government agencies published a joint factsheet urging owners of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems to harden them after grocery-store and military-base fridge attacks that spoiled large amounts of food. Advice is largely standard OT hygiene (reduce Internet exposure, isolate OT, credential security, patching) and applies beyond refrigeration.
Zyxel GS1900 Out-of-Bounds Write Exploited (CVE-2026-107441)

Zyxel released firmware updates for GS1900 series switches fixing an out-of-bounds write that is being exploited in the wild. Binarly found a Python exploit in a malware repository; attacks steal configuration data including hashed passwords. The advisory says the attacker needs network access. Patch to 2.90 Patch 3 builds.

show_notes.heading: Today's Stormcast covers honeypot scans for leftover email test scripts, HD Moore's runZero oobscan for out-of-band management interfaces, a critical apt signature-bypass flaw (CVE-2026-109518), and unpatched SonicWall GMS end-of-life vulnerabilities.
The Classics Return: Vulnerable E-Mail Scripts

Internet Storm Center honeypots are seeing probes for development email test scripts such as sendmail.php and test-mail.php. Like the classic FormMail script, these can leak environment variables and let attackers send spam through GET or POST parameters, so keep them out of production.
oobscan: Scan for Out-of-Band Management Interfaces
HD Moore's runZero oobscan hunts exposed BMC, IPMI, SNMP, and IP KVM style out-of-band management interfaces and flags known vulnerabilities on those devices rather than only listing open ports.
apt Signature Bypass (CVE-2026-109518)

A critical flaw in Debian's apt package manager can skip signature verification when a package web server returns crafted error responses, letting an on-path attacker inject malicious packages over HTTP. Prefer HTTPS where your distribution allows it; Ubuntu still often uses HTTP by default. Debian and Ubuntu have published updates for CVE-2026-109518.
SonicWall GMS End of Life: Unpatched File Read and SQL Injection

SonicWall Global Management System (GMS) 9.5.2 and earlier are end of life, and SonicWall will not fix an unauthenticated file read (CVE-2026-109593) or an authenticated SQL injection (CVE-2026-109594). Migration to Network Security Manager (NSM) is the vendor path forward.

show_notes.heading: Today's episode covers attacks that switch supermarket and military commissary freezers into defrost mode, active exploitation of the Node-RED flaw in Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 devices, the compromised cPGuard anti-malware update channel, and Calif's iPhone exploit that works despite Lockdown Mode.
Refrigerator Exploits: Hacked Freezers Switched to Defrost Mode

Attackers have hit refrigeration controllers at hundreds of supermarkets in France and several other European countries, and U.S. investigators are treating August freezer failures at U.S. military commissaries as a suspected cyberattack. The attackers switch freezers into defrost mode, heating them to about 50 C (122 F) and spoiling the food. How the systems were breached is still unclear, though weak default passwords on internet-exposed controllers have been reported.
To help build a honeypot that emulates these devices, please contact me at jullrich-at-sans.edu if you can provide access to one of these refrigeration controllers.
Exploitation Targeting Node-RED on Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 (CVE-2026-58115)

VulnCheck caught attackers exploiting CVE-2026-58115, a missing authentication flaw (CVSS 10.0) in the Node-RED admin interface of Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced industrial devices, to deploy flows that use wget or curl to download a Linux bot. Siemens patched the flaw in August with version 4.3.4.1. Update, or uninstall or harden Node-RED, and keep industrial control systems (ICS) off the internet.
cPGuard Security Advisory: Update Channel Compromise

OPSSHIELD says an attacker used stolen credentials to access the update servers for cPGuard, its anti-malware product for cPanel and shared hosting servers. On November 2, cPGuard versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 delivered a malicious script that collected /etc/shadow, MySQL configuration, root shell history, and SSH files. Update to 5.88.25 or later, check the install log for affected versions, rotate credentials, and review the indicators of compromise in the advisory.
iPhone 18 Pro Exploited via AirDrop with Lockdown Mode Enabled

Security firm Calif released a video showing an iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode enabled being fully compromised after the user accepted a malicious PDF sent via AirDrop. Calif has not published technical details, so users who rely on Lockdown Mode should not accept unexpected AirDrop files.

show_notes.heading: Today's episode covers how to detect multipath TCP in your network, attacks stealing Bitcoin and Litecoin from outdated BTCPay Server installs, Barracuda patches for an authorization bypass and command injection in Email Security Gateway and other appliances, and Synology's warning about ransomware hitting outdated DSM devices.
Multipath TCP: Use and Detection

Multipath TCP (MPTCP), back in the news because of the Linux vulnerability CVE-2026-98432, is identified by TCP option 30 and is most commonly used by iOS devices connecting to Apple's 17.0.0.0/8 network for Siri and Apple Music. The diary explains the MPTCP subtypes and how to spot them with Wireshark, tcpdump, Suricata and Zeek.
Security Incident Affecting BTCPay Server 2.4.1 and Earlier

Attackers stole Bitcoin and Litecoin from hot wallets on BTCPay Server instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier by exploiting a vulnerability fixed in 2.4.2 (August 7, 2026). BTCPay recommends that affected operators sweep remaining funds to a new wallet, rebuild on a fresh server, and replace any exposed credentials.
Pre-Authentication Authorization Bypass and Command Injection Vulnerabilities in Certain Barracuda Products

Barracuda patched an authorization bypass (CVE-2026-116606, CVSS 9.3) affecting the Email Security Gateway (ESG) and a command injection (CVE-2026-111560, CVSS 8.6) affecting ESG, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF, WAF Control Center and Web Security Gateway. Chained on ESG, they can give an attacker with access to the admin interface root access, so keep admin interfaces off the internet.
Synology urges users to update DSM following ransomware attacks on outdated DSM versions

Synology warns that ransomware attackers are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 (Synology-SA-24:20) on devices still running outdated versions of DSM (DiskStation Manager). Update DSM now and enable automatic updates.

SANS Stormcast Monday, November 2nd, 2026: OneNote Bulk Extraction; Trojanized Claude Code Extension in Cursor Marketplace; Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days (CVE-2026-111357); Android SMS of Death

show_notes.heading: Didier Stevens adds bulk JSON extraction to his OneNote analysis tool, a trojanized Anthropic Claude Code extension in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace installs an SSH backdoor, Ivanti patches two more exploited Connect Secure zero-days, an Android "SMS of Death" proof of concept is public, and a Linux kernel Multipath TCP (MPTCP) mitigation update.
OneNote File Extraction

Didier Stevens added a --jsonoutput option to his onedump.py tool, so embedded attachments from many OneNote (.one) files can be extracted in one run instead of one file at a time. Combined with myjson-filter.py, all embedded files are written to disk named by their SHA-256 hash.
Trojanized Claude Code Extension in Cursor's Marketplace

Malicious versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 of the Anthropic.claude-code extension for Windows and macOS were available in the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace on October 29; they were not built by Anthropic. The extension adds an attacker SSH key, installs persistence, and tries to open a reverse SSH tunnel (that step fails on most hosts without admin rights). Cursor shut down the marketplace during cleanup and published indicators of compromise and detection and remediation scripts.
Ivanti Connect Secure Update and Exploit Details

Ivanti updated its October 13 Connect Secure advisory (CVE-2026-104935, authentication bypass) with fixes for two more vulnerabilities exploited in the same chain: CVE-2026-111357, missing authentication for a critical function allowing escalation to root (CVSS 8.8), and CVE-2026-118527, file uploads to predictable locations. Volexity describes how the three zero-days were chained for unauthenticated root code execution; update to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 even if you patched on October 13.
SMS of Death

A working proof of concept is now public for the "SMS of Death": a single malformed Wireless Application Protocol (WAP) Push SMS crashes com.android.phone, dropping active calls with no user interaction. Google fixed this denial of service in the October 2026 Android security update for Android 14 through 17.
Linux Multipath TCP Vulnerability Update

A follow-up on Friday's Linux kernel remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-98432): the demonstrated exploit needs Multipath TCP enabled and a listening socket. Many distributions have shipped kernel updates; until you can patch, setting the sysctl net.mptcp.enabled=0 disables MPTCP.
